lede: The real documents from DoW and WarU, each with a simple picture version. Documents marked "In this file" open without internet.

hub.title: DPCAP Contract Policy: Workforce Development
hub.note: The official page that lists these documents. Newer versions appear there first.

docs.title: CON 3990V User Experience Roadmap
docs.summary: The 15 steps from "ready to test" to "result on your transcript", with the rules for changing a date and testing again. Page 5 shows a sample score report.

docs.title: CON 3990V User Experience Roadmap Flowchart
docs.summary: The same 15 steps on one color-coded page: who does each step, and what happens after a pass or a fail.

docs.title: Contracting Certification Exam FAQs
docs.summary: 18 answers: the pass mark, the questions per topic, test center or online, retakes, extra training after a fail, and the 3-year grace period.

docs.title: Contracting Professional certification standard
docs.summary: The official list: 5 courses, the exam, 12 months of experience, no degree requirement, then 80 CL hours every 2 years.

docs.title: Contracting Certification Change for FY27 (CON 7300V)
docs.summary: From 1 October 2026, CON 7300V Price Analysis is a required course, taken after CON 1300V.

docs.title: DoW Contracting Competency Model
docs.summary: The table the exam is built on: the guiding principles, the three phases of a contract, their competencies and the job tasks under each.

docs.title: Contracting Competency Model Narrative
docs.summary: The long version (32 pages): what each guiding principle, phase and competency means, explained in words.

docs.title: DoD Contracting Competency Model Narrative (first edition)
docs.summary: The first edition, still linked from the Career Field Model. It explains the model and gives sample assessments for a new contracting professional. Use the 2024 versions for the exam.

docs.title: Contracting Specialty Competencies
docs.summary: An Excel file of specialty areas beyond the basics, such as contingency, construction, A-E and pricing. Not on the exam.

docs.title: DoW Contracting Career Field Model
docs.summary: Your whole career on one page: typical jobs, credentials, graduate schools and leader programs, from contract specialist to senior leader.

docs.title: Workforce Development and Continuous Learning Recommendations for 2025
docs.summary: Spend at least 40 of your 80 continuous learning hours on contracting topics for your job, and plan them in your IDP.

docs.title: Professional Currency and Continuous Learning Credit Guide
docs.summary: How many continuous learning points each kind of learning earns, and the limits. WarU keeps the same chart online.

docs.title: Defense Acquisition Credentials: Contracting
docs.summary: The contracting credentials (CCON). Short, job-focused training. Encouraged, not required.

docs.title: On-the-Job Training Tool for Contract Specialists
docs.summary: A spreadsheet of sample job tasks for each competency. You and your supervisor rate each task from 1 to 3.

docs.title: Training Plan Framework for Pricing Professionals
docs.summary: Pricing training and resources to grow after CON 7300V.

docs.title: Contracting Certification Reciprocity MOU FAQs
docs.summary: DoW's certification and the civilian FAC-C (Professional) count as equal. The continuous learning rules differ: 80 hours versus 100.

docs.title: Reciprocity MOU: FAC-C (Professional) and the DoD Contracting Professional Certification
docs.summary: The signed agreement behind reciprocity (signed 16 October 2023).

docs.title: DoDI 5000.66, Defense Acquisition Workforce program (Change 3)
docs.summary: The DoD rule behind it all: who needs certification, the 3-year grace period, waivers, and 80 CL hours every 2 years.

docs.title: Contracting Workforce Functional Integration Team (CON FIT) Charter
docs.summary: The team that advises on the certification rules, the exam, the competency model and continuous learning, and who sits on it.

docs.title: Contracting Officer Warranting Program Model
docs.summary: A model offices can use to select, appoint (SF 1402) and end contracting officer warrants. Your Army program sets the real rules.

docs.title: Transition Plan for the DoD Contracting Professional Certification Program
docs.summary: How people moved from the old Level I-III certifications to the single Professional certification in 2022.

docs.title: Restructuring of the Certification Program for the Contracting Functional Area
docs.summary: The memo that created one Professional certification with an exam.

docs.title: Back-to-Basics Implementation
docs.summary: Put Back-to-Basics into effect: fewer certification hours, more learning on the job and through credentials.

docs.title: Back-to-Basics for the Defense Acquisition Workforce
docs.summary: The memo that started Back-to-Basics and merged the acquisition career fields into six functional areas, one of them Contracting.

docs.title: Elimination of the 24-Semester Credit Business Hour Qualification Requirement
docs.summary: Removed the old rule of 24 business credit hours for DoD contracting jobs. A bachelor's degree is still required for 1102 civilians.

docs.title: 2024 Acquisition and Sustainment Workforce Framework
docs.summary: Listed on the DPCAP page, but its link returned "not found" on 28 Oct 2026. Ask your DACM office for a copy.

steps.title: Get ready
steps.line: You can test when you are coded in contracting and your supervisor agrees.

steps.title: Apply in AITAS
steps.line: Ask for CON 3990V just like a course. Army: AITAS. Navy: eDACM. Air Force: ACQ Now. 4th Estate: DATMS.

steps.title: Two approvals
steps.line: Your supervisor approves, then your Acquisition Training Office (ATO).
steps.no: Not approved? Fix the problem and apply again when you are eligible.

steps.title: Sent to Pearson
steps.line: Automatic. ATRRS tells WarU, and WarU sends your name and WarU ID to Pearson every day.

steps.title: "Authorization to Test" email
steps.line: Pearson emails you a link to its WarU page, usually within 24 hours.

steps.title: Book your exam
steps.line: Make a Pearson account on the WarU page, then pick a date and a place.

steps.title: Confirmation email
steps.line: No email means the booking did not finish. Go back and finish it.

steps.title: Two reminders
steps.line: Pearson reminds you 3 days and 1 day before your exam.

steps.title: Test day
steps.line: 150 questions in 3 hours. Closed book. Bring your photo ID.

steps.title: Score report
steps.line: You see your score right away: one total, plus a score for each of the 4 parts of the exam.

steps.title: Result goes to your records
steps.line: Pearson sends results to WarU every day. WarU updates AITAS and ATRRS every night.

pass.title: Passed
lines: Your pass shows on your WarU transcript (the sample report says within 3 business days).
WarU does not print a certificate for the exam.
Use your WarU transcript or your Pearson score report when you apply for certification.

fail.title: Not passed
lines: You and your supervisor get a letter from WarU.
Before try 2, take CON 3900V (CON 3910 comes first), unless you already took it.

help.title: Questions at any step
lines: The exam, your booking or your result: email scheduling@waru.edu.
Your Pearson account or a test center: Pearson VUE customer service, 877-269-8108.

choice.title: Test center
choice.line: Pass rate about 4% higher. Search "Military Community" for a test center on a base.

choice.title: Online (OnVUE)
choice.line: Use a personal computer: most government computers block the software. Run the system check first. Quiet room, clear desk, webcam.

rules.title: The 48-hour rule
rules.line: More than 48 hours before: change or cancel it yourself in Pearson. Less than 48 hours: your supervisor emails scheduling@waru.edu.

rules.title: Reschedule, do not cancel
items: Reschedule: free, as many times as you need inside your 90 days
Cancel without a new date: uses 1 of your 3 tries
No-show: counts like a failed try, and the Government still pays

rules.title: The 90-day window
rules.line: No exam within 90 days? Your authorization ends. Wait 30 days, then apply again.

rules.title: Your name must match
rules.line: The name on your ID must match Pearson exactly. If it does not, email scheduling@waru.edu with proof before you book.

rules.title: Cancel in two places
rules.line: Cancel in AITAS and in Pearson. Cancelling in only one does not count.

rules.title: Need an accommodation?
rules.line: Set disability to "Yes" in your AITAS profile before you apply. WarU then explains the process.

chips: The 12 months start on your first try

rows.must: Take CON 3900V before your next try (CON 3910 comes first). Already took it? You do not need it again.
rows.should: Read your score report and study your lowest part.
Review CON 3910 and CON 3900V and your score report again.

rows.must: Review your feedback and both prep courses. Your agency checks your steps before you test again.

rows.should: Possible in the 12 months that start one year after your first failed try. Your DACM can approve more tries, case by case.

attempts.note: Your agency (your supervisor and training office) can add its own rules, such as more training, waiting time or counseling.

grace.goalLabel: Many units: courses and exam by month 6

cards.title: Promoted inside contracting?
cards.line: The clock keeps running. It does not start over.

cards.title: Running late?
cards.line: A waiver can let you stay in the job longer. It never gives you the certification. Ask early.

cards.title: Condition of employment
cards.line: Without the certification and without a waiver, you can face employment actions.

tiles: At the end you price a realistic case
Exam data showed pricing as the biggest area to improve
cases: Your Component decides. DoW leadership expects you to take it.
People working on their certification get first priority.

rails: NPS MS in Contract Management, National Defense University, Senior Service College Fellowship
DCELP, ELDP, DSLDP, White House LDP, Vanguard

facts: The day you enter an acquisition position, not the day you are certified. Your Component sets the 2-year dates.
DPCAP asks for at least 40 of your 80 hours on contracting topics for your job.
Follow your Component's process. Points for WarU events do not post by themselves; request them.

kinds.title: Formal training
kinds.eg: WarU courses (points listed in the iCatalog) · college: 15 per semester hour · 10 per CEU

kinds.title: Informal learning
kinds.eg: Webinars, videos, workshops: 1 per hour · reading: 1 per hour, up to 4 per item · conferences: up to 24

kinds.title: Professional activities
kinds.eg: Non-DAWIA certificate or license: 10 to 30 · teaching: 2 per hour, up to 20 · writing: up to 20

kinds.title: Experience
kinds.eg: On-the-job assignments: up to 20 · rotations: up to 40 · mentoring: up to 5 a year

cl.source: Points: WarU Continuous Learning Point Credit chart and the iCatalog course pages, checked 28 Oct 2026.

facts: DoW: 80 hours every 2 years. Civilian agencies (OFPP): 100 hours every 2 years since May 2024.
Your DoW certification counts. Ask the new agency's career manager.
Coming to DoW from a civilian agency?
Your DACM can accept FAC-C (Professional). Without it, meet all DoW requirements.
Open it when you start the job, and review it at least twice a year.
Tasks for each technical and professional competency. Your office can add its own.
You and your supervisor rate each task: 1 lowest, 3 highest, or N/A.
Your supervisor signs completed tasks. It also helps show your 12 months of experience.

steps: Training, experience, education and judgment are checked (FAR 1.603-2). Often a test, an interview or a CORB.
Your warrant is an SF 1402 Certificate of Appointment. It states your limits.
By letter: for example reassignment, leaving the job or poor performance. Never backdated.
warrant.baseline: The model's minimum for a warrant: the DoW Contracting Professional certification, a bachelor's degree (1102s and military equivalents) and 2 years of contracting experience. Your Army warrant program sets the real rules.
